title: I made Intel Desk: a live geopolitical dashboard that scores its own sources and tracks ships through the Strait of Hormuz. Free.
author: Internal-Estimate-21
selftext:
I trade energy and macro and built this for my own workflow, then opened it up. It pulls 199 named news and OSINT sources, tiers each one A to D by reliability, and refuses to call anything confirmed until a second source or the market backs it. When two sources contradict each other, it keeps both on screen instead of hiding one behind a clean summary.

It also tracks vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz in real time (transit direction, ships going dark, floating storage) and rolls it into a corridor-pressure index, and it cross-checks market prices across providers.

Everything is auditable: there is a public replay archive and a scorecard, so you can check what it called and when. On 23 March it logged Trump postponing strikes on Iran 88 seconds before mainstream coverage, with Brent moving about 12% over the next ninety minutes.

Free, web and iOS, no signup wall to look: [https://www.inteldesk.app](https://www.inteldesk.app). Happy to answer anything about how it is built.
